principle: Books and courses are evidence containers, not knowledge nodes. NisabaDB will extract only the ideas a goal actually needs, compare alternate routes, and publish a compressed route only after review.

materials.title: Prealgebra 2e

access.note: Free web and PDF access; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. OpenStax separately restricts ingestion into generative-AI offerings, so NisabaDB records metadata and links unless permission is obtained.

materials.plainLanguageRole: A repair kit for fractions, signed numbers, equations, units, and basic geometry. A learner tests out of anything already known.
materials.compressionNote: Use as a diagnostic bank, never as a cover-to-cover requirement.

materials.title: Algebra and Trigonometry 2e

access.note: Free web and PDF access; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Full-text AI processing requires separate attention to OpenStax's current terms.

materials.plainLanguageRole: A broad source bank for equations, functions, graphs, logarithms, systems, sequences, counting, and trigonometry.
materials.compressionNote: Select only the sections required by a later goal; compare them with the shorter Active Prelude route.

materials.title: Active Prelude to Calculus

access.note: Free HTML, PDF, and source under CC BY-SA 4.0.

materials.plainLanguageRole: A shorter route through the algebra, functions, and trigonometry that calculus actually uses.
materials.compressionNote: This is an early test of whether one purpose-built route can replace much of separate algebra and trigonometry courses.

materials.title: Mathematical Reasoning: Writing and Proof

access.note: Free PDF under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Teaches how to read, construct, and clearly write a proof instead of assuming that skill appears automatically.
materials.compressionNote: Proof language is a shared foundation; teach it once and reuse it across every branch.

materials.title: Active Calculus — Single Variable

access.note: Free HTML, PDF, and source under CC BY-SA 4.0.

materials.plainLanguageRole: An activity-led source for limits, derivatives, integrals, and the few continuous ideas later mathematics genuinely needs.
materials.compressionNote: Make only goal-required calculus nodes mandatory; finite mathematics should not inherit calculus by habit.

materials.title: Mathematics for Computer Science

access.note: Free through MIT OpenCourseWare; the linked textbook revision is CC BY-SA 3.0.

materials.plainLanguageRole: The first common core joining proof, counting, graphs, recurrences, asymptotics, and finite probability.
materials.compressionNote: Treat it as an integration source, not a 900-page assignment; avoid reteaching its proof and probability core elsewhere.

materials.title: Linear Algebra

access.note: Free PDF, source, solutions, videos, and Sage lab under GFDL or CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Starts with solving systems by computation, then turns those procedures into vector spaces and linear maps.
materials.compressionNote: Teach computation before abstraction, then reuse the same matrix language in probability, algorithms, and representation theory.

materials.title: Introduction to Probability

access.note: Free MIT OpenCourseWare videos and notes; license and exceptions must be checked item by item.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Builds probability from experiments and uncertainty through conditioning, expectation, concentration, and limit behavior.
materials.compressionNote: Begin with finite probability; delay density and integration machinery until a goal needs continuous distributions.

materials.title: Algorithms

access.note: Free PDF under CC BY 4.0.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Turns proofs, recurrences, graphs, and combinatorics into procedures a computer can execute.
materials.compressionNote: Reuse the discrete-math core and add only the computational design patterns.

materials.title: Introduction to Theoretical Computer Science

access.note: Free to read under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; NisabaDB must link and write independent explanations.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Introduces what computers can do efficiently, how reductions transfer difficulty, and why randomness can help.
materials.compressionNote: Carry the beginner complexity route here; consult advanced complexity references only for missing precision.

materials.title: Visual Group Theory

access.note: Publisher-controlled book; use as a cited evidence source, not as reusable text.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Begins group theory with visible symmetries, multiplication tables, and diagrams rather than a wall of definitions.
materials.compressionNote: Use concrete transformations as the on-ramp to executable algebra.

materials.title: Group Explorer

access.note: Free web application; source is LGPL v3.0.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Lets a learner click, draw, and test small groups before manipulating the definitions symbolically.
materials.compressionNote: Every early abstract group concept should receive a small manipulable witness.

materials.title: Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications

access.note: Free HTML, PDF, and source under GNU Free Documentation License 1.2 or later.

materials.plainLanguageRole: The main algebra source: groups, actions, rings, fields, and applications paired with executable Sage work.
materials.compressionNote: Do not inherit its chapter order; express structures through operations, programs, invariants, and decompositions.

materials.title: SageMath PREP Tutorials

access.note: Free documentation under CC BY-SA 3.0; SageMath software is GPL.

materials.plainLanguageRole: A low-programming notebook layer for trying algebra and linear algebra immediately.
materials.compressionNote: Pair computation with each conceptual node instead of postponing it to a separate software course.

materials.title: GAP — A Tutorial

access.note: Free documentation and GPL v2-or-later core software.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Turns generators, permutations, subgroups, maps, character tables, and representations into executable objects.
materials.compressionNote: Use GAP to expose what an abstract definition lets us compute, while still explaining the mathematics behind the command.

materials.title: Notes on Computational Group Theory

access.note: Free official PDF with educational-use permission; no standard open adaptation license is stated.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Explains the algorithms hidden under group-computation commands: orbits, stabilizers, rewriting, and recognition.
materials.compressionNote: This is evidence for rebuilding group theory around algorithms, not a novice reading assignment.

materials.title: Introduction to Representation Theory

access.note: Free MIT OpenCourseWare notes under the license stated by OCW; the related AMS book has separate posting restrictions.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Explains a representation as a group action by matrices, then develops decomposition, characters, and the symmetric group.
materials.compressionNote: Select the finite-group route; quivers, Lie theory, and homological algebra are not default prerequisites.

materials.title: The Symmetric Group

access.note: Commercial or library access; no open adaptation license.

materials.plainLanguageRole: The compact target source joining representations of the symmetric group, tableaux algorithms, and symmetric functions.
materials.compressionNote: This is one strong current route to the dictatorship paper, not a claim of optimality.

materials.title: SageMath: Representations of the Symmetric Group

access.note: Documentation under CC BY-SA 3.0; SageMath software is GPL.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Computes tableaux, Young symmetrizers, hook lengths, and small representation matrices so the abstract theory has visible examples.
materials.compressionNote: Require executable low-rank witnesses for every representation-theory abstraction where practical.

materials.title: Young Tableaux

access.note: Commercial or library access; no open adaptation license.

materials.plainLanguageRole: An alternate route beginning more directly from tableaux and combinatorics before connecting to representations and geometry.
materials.compressionNote: Compare its self-contained combinatorial path against the Sagan–Etingof route instead of silently adding both.

materials.title: Analysis of Boolean Functions

access.note: Author-hosted PDF is free for noncommercial personal use; other rights are retained.

materials.plainLanguageRole: The central technical source for Fourier expansion, influence, noise, hypercontractivity, Gaussian comparison, and testing.
materials.compressionNote: Import only the chapters used by a target theorem; keep general-domain and Gaussian machinery on demand.

materials.title: Introduction to Property Testing

access.note: Published edition is commercial; author drafts are free to read but copyright is retained and reposting is restricted.

materials.plainLanguageRole: Introduces algorithms that inspect only a tiny part of an object, including dictatorship and junta testing.
materials.compressionNote: Share probability and algorithm nodes with the common core; add Fourier analysis only when a tester uses it.

materials.title: Boolean Function Analysis

access.note: Free official notes; the author's site states all rights reserved.

materials.plainLanguageRole: A short bridge from Boolean-cube analysis to invariance and analysis on a fixed-size slice.
materials.compressionNote: Use chiefly its slice and invariance sections instead of duplicating O'Donnell's Boolean-cube core.

materials.title: Probabilistically Checkable Proofs

access.note: Free MIT OpenCourseWare notes; the license and any marked exceptions must be checked item by item.

materials.plainLanguageRole: A direct advanced route through PCP composition, long codes, dictatorship tests, Unique Games, and hardness.
materials.compressionNote: Keep this outside the common core; activate only for the hardness application branch.

materials.title: Measure, Integration & Real Analysis

access.note: Open-access book under CC BY-NC 4.0.

materials.plainLanguageRole: A repair source when a proof truly needs measure, integration, Hilbert spaces, or rigorous continuous probability.
materials.compressionNote: Reference on demand: it must not block finite Boolean-function analysis merely because conventional courses put analysis first.

goals.title: Write and understand a first proof
goals.description: Start at the learner's actual arithmetic level, then acquire only the algebra and proof language needed to make a rigorous argument.

goals.title: Build the first mathematical common core
goals.description: Join proof, discrete mathematics, linear algebra, probability, and algorithms without repeating their shared foundations.

goals.title: Reach computational algebra
goals.description: Learn algebra through visible transformations and executable structures, then uncover the algorithms behind the software.

goals.title: Reach Young diagrams and symmetric-group representations
goals.description: Move from matrices and group actions to partitions, tableaux, representations, and executable low-rank examples.

goals.title: Prepare for dictatorship testing
goals.description: Combine the current Young-diagram route with finite probability, Boolean analysis, property testing, and complexity. This is a candidate route, not the claimed minimum.

goals.title: Prepare for multislice invariance and hardness
goals.description: Add slice analysis and the optional PCP branch to the Boolean-analysis and symmetric-group foundations used by the current research paper.

compressionCandidates.title: One purpose-built common core
compressionCandidates.hypothesis: Selected algebra and function nodes, one explicit proof bridge, and Mathematics for Computer Science may replace large repeated portions of traditional algebra, trigonometry, proof, discrete-math, and introductory-probability sequences.

compressionCandidates.title: Abstract algebra as executable structure
compressionCandidates.hypothesis: The reusable pattern structure → structure-preserving programs → invariants → decomposition can unify early group, linear, module, and representation theory while computation supplies concrete witnesses.

compressionCandidates.title: Compare the Young-diagram routes
compressionCandidates.hypothesis: A representation-first route through Etingof and Sagan and a tableaux-first route through Fulton may have different prerequisite costs; both should be measured before either is declared minimal.

compressionCandidates.title: Keep finite analysis finite
compressionCandidates.hypothesis: Discrete probability and linear algebra may support much of Boolean-function analysis without making a full measure-theory course a mandatory ancestor; continuous analysis can be loaded only where a proof uses it.
